Yeast_Cell_Shape: Oval, subglobose to pyriform, thin-walled (0.2 - 0.4 µm)
Yeast_Budding_Pattern: Single narrow-based polar bud; typically clustered intracellularly within host macrophage phagolysosomes
Intracellular_Niche_and_Tropism: Reticuloendothelial system (alveolar macrophages, Kupffer cells, splenic histiocytes, bone marrow)
Mold_Microconidia_um: 2.0 - 4.0 µm, unicellular, pyriform to globose, smooth/verrucose on lateral pedicels (infectious aerosolized propagules)
Mold_Tuberculate_Macroconidia_um: 8.0 - 15.0 µm, thick-walled, spherical, covered with diagnostic prominent finger-like tuberculate projections
Mold_Hyphae_um: 1.5 - 2.5 µm, septate, hyaline, highly branched mycelium
Colony_Morphology_25C_Mold: Slow-growing (2-4 weeks on SDA); white-to-buff or tan cottony/woolly aerial mycelium with pale yellow/brown reverse
Colony_Morphology_37C_Yeast: Cream to beige, moist, glabrous to wrinkled, pasty bacterial-like yeast colonies on BHI / Blood agar
Histopathology_Staining_Profile: GMS positive (deep brown/black wall), PAS positive (magenta), Wright-Giemsa (characteristic clear pseudo-halo due to cell shrinkage), Calcofluor White (bright UV fluorescence of cell wall chitin)
Antifungal_Susceptibility_ECVs: Amphotericin B (MIC: 0.03-0.25 µg/mL; Gold Standard), Itraconazole (MIC: 0.015-0.06 µg/mL; 1st-line maintenance), Voriconazole/Posaconazole/Isavuconazole (Active); Intrinsic Resistance to Echinocandins (Caspofungin/Micafungin)
Clinical_Presentation_Syndrome: Classic histoplasmosis: Acute/chronic pulmonary, progressive disseminated (bone marrow, spleen, liver, adrenals, mucocutaneous)
Study_Title: Genome Sequences Reveal Cryptic Speciation in the Human Pathogen Histoplasma capsulatum
Study_Authors: Sepúlveda VE, Márquez R, Turissini DA, Goldman WE, Matute DR
